page.layout: One column of running text, set full width. Small marginal marks and fragments at the left edge, at about lines 17–19 and 26–31. No right margin text. The catchword stands at the foot, right of centre.

main_text.p: enim spreverant nuper optima & fidis[?]. fima ipsius monita, & soli è Græcis injuriosè de eo locuti fuerant. Verum is posthabitis[?] contumeliis cum in castra venisset, pro obsessis intercessit apud confulem[?], & obsidione solutà inducias iis confecit tanti temporis, per quod Romam legatos deprecatores mittere, iique cum responso in patriam redire possent. Profectis verò Romam legatis, & in senatu auditis, post multam actionem tandem tale responsum dedit: oportere Ætolos aut senatus arbitrio libero se permittere, aut mille talenta pendere, & simul eosdem amicos vel inimicos cum Romanis habere: nec impetrari à petentibus potuit, ut quam rerum arbitrium permitti sibi poteret, senatus profiteretur. Iussi autem legati sunt eodem illo die urbe, intra dies xv Italiâ excedere. Succensebant quippe Ætolis Romani vehementius tanquàm indomitæ genti, qui odio Romani nominis Antiochum nuper in Europam exciverant, & vastationum xcædium innumerarum caufam dederant. Inter quos Acilius consul xliii principes Ætolicæ gentis, & in his Democritum illum, qui castra in Italiâ se sofiturum[?], atque iis Quinctio se responsurum, urum jactaverat, ejusdemque fratrem [illegible, ~3 letters] in

page.notes: Left margin: small fragments ("ià", "io", "E3") and a red overlay at about lines 17–19 and 28–31 are not clearly legible; only the marks noted above are given. Line 1 "fidif." read as "fidis" (long s). "confulem" printed as seen (u vowel), possibly a misprint for "consulem". "posthabitis" and "sofiturum" are doubtful readings. Line 31 begins "urum", the word is cut by the scan edge. Page number "320" at the head is uncertain (read as "ƨ20"). Printed "Democritum" is divided "De-/mocritum" across lines 28–29.
